stem: Meena shines a torch onto a plane mirror fixed on the wall of her classroom. She holds a white sheet of card so that the incident ray and the normal to the mirror both lie along the sheet. What must be true for the reflected ray to appear on the same sheet?

options.text: The reflected ray always lies in the same plane as the incident ray and the normal, so it will appear on the sheet
The reflected ray lies in a different plane from the incident ray, so it cannot appear on the sheet
The reflected ray lies in the same plane as the incident ray but not the normal, so it may not appear on the sheet
The reflected ray can lie in any plane, so bending the sheet makes no difference to where it appears

teacher.key_rationale: The law of reflection states that the incident ray, the normal at the point of incidence, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane. Since the incident ray and normal are already on the sheet, the reflected ray must also lie on the sheet, making A correct. B and C misstate the plane relationships; D drops the same-plane condition, the intended trap for a student who ignores the stated law.
